annotation.title_clean: If Androids Dream, Are They More Than Sheep?: Westworld, Robots and Legal Rights
annotation.title_en: If Androids Dream, Are They More Than Sheep?: Westworld, Robots and Legal Rights
annotation.venue: Dialogue: The Interdisciplinary Journal of Popular Culture and Pedagogy
annotation.summary_en: Essay using HBO's Westworld to examine whether sophisticated androids should receive legal protections like persons, drawing on analogies to animal and corporate rights. It argues a legal framework protecting companion androids will become necessary and suggests classroom uses of the series.
key_provisions_or_claims: Legal protections should be extended to androids once they reach sufficient sophistication (feeling, consciousness, agency).
Animal cruelty laws and corporate rights serve as analogies for non-human legal protection.
Androids capable of killing raise questions of legal responsibility and consequences.
Personhood is tied to experience of pain, empathy and free will.
Westworld is a useful classroom tool for discussing robot rights.
